Cautiously positive, with an added note of vigilance from the FSR. The Committee hiked the federal funds rate and signaled gradual normalization while emphasizing a symmetric 2 percent inflation objective and close monitoring of below-target inflation—consistent with anchoring expectations and the flat Phillips curve dynamics. That supports a measured, credibility-preserving path.

The Financial Stability Report tempers this by noting accommodative financial conditions alongside elevated asset valuations/compressed risk premiums and some buildup in business-sector leverage, even as core funding risks and bank capital/liquidity remain solid. This mix suggests supportive near-term growth and employment but a somewhat higher medium-term vulnerability backdrop, warranting a slightly more guarded read than a pure policy-hike signal would imply.

Net: moderately constructive on activity and labor, tempered by undershooting inflation and FSR-flagged valuation/leverage vulnerabilities. Adjusting for the FSR, the tone skews a bit more cautious than the initial read. 

sentiment score = 0.24
